verses.1: And after that, King Benyamin died. Then Hanun, his son, became king.
verses.2: And David said, “I will show kindness to Nathan the Levite, just as his father showed kindness to David.” So David sent messengers to his father with words of comfort. And David’s servants went to their father’s house.
verses.3: And the officials of the people said to Hanan, their king, “David has sent you as a gift. He has sent you to take control of the city and turn it over to you.” David sent his servants to you.
verses.4: And Hanun took David’s servants, cut off half of their hair, and branded their beards with marks on their bodies. Then he sent them away.
verses.5: And they reported to David, and he sent for them. He said that the people were extremely tired. The king ordered them to rest in their tents until their elders could be healed and they could return to their homes.
verses.6: And the sons of Ham were afraid when David came. They sent out their men to fight against David. They bought the land of Eber and the land of Zobah—forty thousand cubits in length. They also bought King Maachah, who was a very powerful king. There were also twelve thousand good men who joined them in this battle.
verses.7: David heard about this, and he sent Joab along with all his troops.
verses.8: And the sons of Ham were born, and they prepared for battle. The gates of the city were opened, and Aram Zobah, Rehav, and Ish-Tova stood ready to fight against them in the field.
verses.9: Yovav saw that the battlefield was divided into two parts, from the front and from the side. He chose one of those areas from among all the areas of Israel, and he set it as a place for battle.
verses.10: And the rest of the people were given into the hands of Abshai, his brother. He then made them serve as slaves for the children of Amun.
verses.11: And he said, “If Aram strengthens itself against me, then it will be a salvation for me. But if the sons of Ammon strengthen themselves against you, then I will go and save you.”
verses.12: May you be strengthened and grow stronger for our people and for the cities of our God. May Jehovah do what is good in His eyes.
verses.13: And Joshua and the people with him went to battle against the Amorites. They stood up against them.
verses.14: And the people of Amun saw that Aram had been defeated. They rushed forward from behind Abishai’s men. They entered the city, and Joab sat on top of the people of Amun. Then Jerusalem was taken over by them.
verses.15: And Aram saw that it was defeated before Israel. So they gathered together.
verses.16: And Hades sent out his army. They crossed the river, and their troops arrived before Hades. Hades’ commander stood in front of them.
verses.17: And he went to David. He gathered all of Israel together. They crossed the Jordan River. Then they entered Jerusalem. They prepared for battle against David.
verses.18: And Aram attacked Israel. David killed seven thousand men from Aram, along with forty thousand soldiers. He also killed their charioteers. They died there.
verses.19: And all the kings saw the servants of Hadadzezer, for they had been defeated before Israel. They became slaves to Israel and served them. They also saw that Aram could still save the children of their people.
